newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down on Tuesday due to profit taking after recent sharp gains, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index fell 1.33 points, or 0.19 percent, to close at 698.40 points. Decliners led advancers by 72 to 61 with 67 issues remained unchanged.
Total turn-over was 566 billion rupiah against 685 billion rupiah on Monday.
"Players took profit not just in big-caps, but also in small-capitalised stocks," one broker said.
"Prices are likely to move in a narrow range on Wednesday, with profit-taking likely to continue in certain stocks," another broker said.
Big-caps Bimantara, Gudang Garam and Bank BNI were among the losers following the profit-taking, brokers said.
Bimantara fell 200 rupiah to 4,000 rupiah despite Tuesday's news reports that the firm had lowered its car prices in order to increase sales volume, brokers said.
Gudang Garam was down 125 rupiah to 10,575 rupiah and most active Bank BNI fell 50 rupiah to 1,600 rupiah.
Brokers, however, said active local buying of certain big-caps on speculation of corporate actions helped to limit the index's fall.
Automobile conglomerate Astra rose 350 rupiah to 7,050 rupiah on market talk that the firm was likely to split its nominal price per share which could further boost liquidity, one broker said.
Astra was not immediately available for comment.
Small property firm Surya Semesta ended down 25 rupiah at 1,175 rupiah in active trading due to profit-taking, brokers said.
Surya had made strong gains recently on market talk that it had been expected to book strong first quarter results and that a foreign firm was expected to buy a stake in the firm.
Surya announced on Tuesday it posted a net profit of 28.28 billion rupiah in the first quarter of 1997 against a net loss of 10.03 billion rupiah in the corresponding period in 1996.
